Pub. 527 (2025) pp. 25-26, Dividing Expenses: a day rented at a fair price is a rental day even if also used personally, so total use is 190 fair days + 12 personal days - 2 days that were both = 200 days, and the rental part is 190/200 = 0.95 (six places 0.950000). Dwelling Unit Used as a Home (p. 26): 12 personal days is not more than 14, so it is not used as a home and the expenses are divided (p. 28, Not used as a home). Each shared cost times 0.95: cleaning 1,000 -> 950.00; insurance 1,200 -> 1,140.00; legal 800 -> 760.00; mortgage 6,000 -> 5,700.00; other interest 400 -> 380.00; repairs 1,500 -> 1,425.00; supplies 300 -> 285.00; taxes 2,000 -> 1,900.00; utilities 1,100 -> 1,045.00; other 500 -> 475.00. No advertising, commissions or management fees were paid, so lines 5, 8 and 11 are 0 (whether rental-only costs are divided is not tested here). No depreciation. Line 20 14,060.00; line 21 = 20,000 - 14,060 = 5,940.00 (i1040se line 21), Schedule E line 24 5,940.00.

Mutation fixture (lane mrental), predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Pub. 527 (2025) pp. 25-26, Dividing Expenses: every personal-use day of rentals a and b was also a fair rental day (a: 5 of 5, b: 12 of 12), and such a day counts as a rental day, so total use is 100 days, all rental: the rental part is 100/100 = 1 and nothing is cut. Since the rental part is 1 or there is no personal use, the result does not depend on whether costs of the rental alone are divided by days. a: advertising 1,000, commissions 600, management 800, no cleaning or legal fees: line 20 2,400.00, line 21 7,600.00. b: advertising 1,000: line 21 9,000.00. c: advertising 1,000, cleaning 700, commissions 600, legal 450, management 800: line 20 3,550.00, line 21 6,450.00. A single-family rental (rents $5,000, active participation) with a $2,000 loss carried over, part of it rental costs carried over from an earlier year's Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 when the owner also used the place as a home. p527 p. 28: that limit applies to expenses carried forward even if the property is not used as a home in the later year; this tool does not apply it, so the prior-year unallowed loss (Form 8582 Part IV (c)) refuses.

rental[a].prior_loss.form: Pub. 527, Worksheet 5-1 (expenses carried over from a year of home use)
rental[a].prior_loss.remedy: Rental costs carried over from an earlier year's Worksheet 5-1, when the place counted as your home, are outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 28, "This limitation will apply to expenses carried forward to another year even if you don’t use the property as your home for that subsequent year"

cases.evidence_note: Mutation fixture (the rental.zero operand of rental.allowed's not-listed alternative, read as rental.p7c_share by the mutant), predicted by hand before running: the inputs of x1sche.f1.profit (rents $18,000, line 21 $1,782.40, a profit). i8582 Part VII is completed only for activities with an overall loss in Part V column (e) or a loss in Part VI column (d), and Part VIII lists the activities of Part VII: this rental has no loss, so Part VII column (a) is $0 (rental.p7_listed false) and its Part VIII loss allowed (rental.allowed) is $0.

BUG-0995, predicted by hand before running: i1040se p. 7, Line 12, interest paid beyond the Form 1098 amount needs Pub. 334 and an attached statement; a Yes to rental.mortgage_excess (asked because mortgage interest was ticked) refuses Schedule E line 12.

rental[a].line12.form: Schedule E, line 12 (mortgage interest beyond Form 1098, with a statement)
rental[a].line12.remedy: Mortgage interest beyond what Form 1098 shows needs a statement explaining the difference and is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 7, Line 12, "If you paid more mortgage interest than is shown on your Form 1098 or similar statement"

cases.evidence_note: BUG-0992, predicted by hand before running: p527 p. 5, the cost of a leasehold bought for rental purposes is deducted in equal parts over the lease term; a Yes to rental.bought_lease refuses Schedule E line 19.

rental[a].line19.form: Schedule E, line 19 (cost of a leasehold bought for rental purposes)
rental[a].line19.remedy: The cost of a lease you bought, which is spread over the lease's term, is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 5, Rental of property, "If you buy a leasehold for rental purposes, you can deduct an equal part of the cost each year over the term of the lease"

cases.evidence_note: BUG-0943, predicted by hand before running: i8582 p. 3, Exceptions, a rental incidental to a trade or business the filer owns an interest in is not a rental activity; a Yes to rental.business_incidental refuses line 21.

rental[a].line21.form: Form 8582 exceptions (rental incidental to a trade or business)
rental[a].line21.remedy: Property mainly used in a business you or your spouse own, and rented for under 2% of its cost or value, is not a rental activity under the passive activity rules and is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 3, Exceptions, "The rental of property is incidental to a trade or business activity if"

cases.evidence_note: BUG-0938, predicted by hand before running: a house rented all 365 days, no personal use, rent $20,000; interest of $1,500 on a home equity loan on the filer's own home whose money was spent on the rental (i1040se p. 6, interest is allocated by tracing the loan proceeds) entered as other interest; property tax $3,000; no buildings listed. Line 13 $1,500, line 16 $3,000, line 20 $4,500, line 21 $20,000 - $4,500 = $15,500.

BUG-0994, predicted by hand before running: a house rented all 365 days at a fair price to the filer's son as his main home (p527 pp. 26-27, not personal use); the filer answers that a relative used it but counts 0 personal days. Not used as a home, no Worksheet 5-1 refusal; the use ratio is 365/365, so insurance of $1,200 is taken whole: line 9 $1,200, line 21 $14,400 - $1,200 = $13,200.

BUG-0953, predicted by hand before running. Single, W-2 wages $160,000. Rental a: line 21 $10,000 - $1,000 = $9,000. Rental b, a house, both actively managed: rent $12,000 less mortgage interest $15,000 and tax $7,000 = -$10,000. Form 8582 has a passive deduction and MAGI $160,000 > $100,000, so the filing exception fails and Form 8582 is required (f8582.required). Rental a is land only (Pub. 925 p. 16, less than 30% of unadjusted basis depreciable), with net passive income $9,000 > 0: recharacterized as nonpassive, refused at rental[a].nondep_income on line 22.

rental[a].line22.form: Form 8582 (rental of nondepreciable property, income recharacterized as nonpassive)
rental[a].line22.remedy: Net income from renting land, or property whose buildings were under 30% of its cost, is treated as nonpassive when Form 8582 limits other losses, and is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 16, Rental of Nondepreciable Property, "less than 30% of the unadjusted basis of the property is subject to depreciation"

cases.evidence_note: Hand-predicted before evaluating. Return bfr.rental.nondep_land_income_refused (land rental a with line 21 $9,000; house b with a $10,000 loss; MAGI $160,000, so no special allowance and Form 8582 required), where a loss of $12,000 from rental a was held back on the 2024 Form 8582 (Part VII column (c)). Rental a's net result with the prior-year loss is a $3,000 loss, so it has no net passive income to recharacterize (p925 p. 16, Rental of Nondepreciable Property, applies to net passive income): rental[a].nondep_gain is $0 and nondep_income false, so line 22 is not refused. All of the $3,000 overall loss is unallowed (no passive income elsewhere, no special allowance), carried forward in Part VII column (c); the $9,000 of the prior-year loss that this year's income absorbs is allowed, so rental a's line 22 is -$9,000.

BUG-0953, predicted by hand before running: rental a alone (land, line 21 $9,000), W-2 $160,000. No passive deduction, so Form 8582 is not required and the land income needs no recharacterization: not refused; Schedule E line 26 $9,000.

BUG-0953, predicted by hand before running. Single, W-2 wages $160,000. Rental a: line 21 $10,000 - $1,000 = $9,000. rental[a].line22.remedy: Net income from renting land, or property whose buildings were under 30% of its cost, is treated as nonpassive when Form 8582 limits other losses, and is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 16, Rental of Nondepreciable Property, "less than 30% of the unadjusted basis of the property is subject to depreciation"

cases.evidence_note: BUG-0953, predicted by hand before running. Single, W-2 wages $160,000. Rental a: line 21 $10,000 - $1,000 = $9,000. Rental b, a house, both actively managed: rent $12,000 less mortgage interest $15,000 and tax $7,000 = -$10,000. Form 8582 has a passive deduction and MAGI $160,000 > $100,000, so the filing exception fails and Form 8582 is required (f8582.required). Rental a is a house whose buildings were 30% or more of its cost: no recharacterization. Form 8582 Part IV: income $9,000, loss $10,000, line 3 -$1,000; MAGI $160,000 >= $150,000 gives no special allowance, so the allowed loss is the passive income, $9,000: rental b line 22 -$9,000 and Schedule E line 26 $9,000 - $9,000 = $0.

Lane rentals (2026-11-24), predicted by hand before running the evaluator: a single-family rental with $12,000 rent and $1,000 property tax; every other screen answer takes its default (No), so the first refusal on the property's line 21 is an earlier return had Form 6198 for it (p925 p. 19: a loss disallowed by the at-risk limits carries to the next year; allowed losses can be recaptured).

rental[a].line21.remedy: A rental with Form 6198 on an earlier return, or a loss held back because amounts were not at risk, can carry that loss into 2025 or owe recapture of losses allowed before; this tool does not prepare Form 6198.

cite.locator: p. 19, At-Risk Limits, "You treat any loss that is disallowed because of the at-risk limits as a deduction from the same activity in the next tax year"

cases.evidence_note: Lane rentals (2026-11-24), predicted by hand before running the evaluator: a single-family rental with $12,000 rent and $1,000 property tax; every other screen answer takes its default (No), so the first refusal on the property's line 21 is it was first offered for rent in 2025 after costs were paid (p527 p. 5: expenses are deductible from the time it is made available for rent).

rental[a].line21.form: Costs paid before a rental was first offered for rent
rental[a].line21.remedy: Costs paid before a property is first offered for rent are not rental expenses of that time; depending on what they are, they are added to its cost, amortized as start-up costs on Form 4562, or not deducted, which this tool does not sort out.

cite.locator: p. 5, Pre-rental expenses, "You can deduct your ordinary and necessary expenses for managing, conserving, or maintaining rental property from the time you make it available for rent"; i4562 p. 18, Startup and organizational costs, "Business startup costs (section 195)"

cases.evidence_note: Lane rentals (2026-11-24), predicted by hand before running the evaluator: a single-family rental with $12,000 rent and $1,000 property tax; every other screen answer takes its default (No), so the first refusal on the property's line 21 is its general business credit (i1040gi p. 116, Lines 6a Through 6z: the credit applies to filers who have rental property); Schedule 3 line 7 also refuses, through s3.business_credit_any, which now counts rentals that claim the credit.

rental[a].line21.remedy: A business credit for a rental (Form 3800) goes on Schedule 3 line 6a; this tool does not prepare it. To go on without the credit, answer No to that question.

cite.locator: p. 116, Lines 6a Through 6z, "See Form 3800 or Pub. 334"

s3.line7.remedy: A business credit (Form 3800) goes on line 6a; this tool does not prepare it.
